projects.name: Somfy
projects.summary: I design the dashboards, the main flows and the design system that six product teams build with.
projects.tagline: One design language for Somfy’s B2B and B2C products.

facts.Scope: Design system, Product design, App design, Web design

projects.intro: Somfy makes smart home and building automation products used around the world. I’ve worked with them as a freelance product designer since April 2023, on both B2B and B2C, and we’re still adding features one after another.
owned: The design system and its component library
projects.team: Six product teams work with the component library, across B2B and B2C.

outcomes.label: product teams using the component library
less time spent on handoff between design and development

chapters.title: Dashboard and order tracking
body: The first goal was to help professional clients read their business data and track their orders.

I redesigned the activity dashboard so yearly performance and order activity are visible at a glance. The new order tracking flow is easier to navigate for people who use it every day: they find things faster and need less help from support.

chapters.title: Product comparator
body: I designed a new way to compare products: you select several and see them side by side.
Installers now choose with more confidence, and the catalogue is easier to browse and understand.

chapters.title: Installer homepage and product variants
body: The new homepage has to be useful from the first click, so the main actions, quick tools and relevant data are laid out in a clear order.
I also reworked the product variant tables to simplify the technical data and make it easier to read. Both pages use the new design system and work across the full Somfy range.

projects.name: Zestia
projects.summary: I worked directly with the CEO and CTO and designed the whole MVP from scratch.
projects.tagline: An MVP for every step of buying a property.

facts.Scope: Design system, Product design, SaaS design, MVP design

projects.intro: Zestia puts the whole property buying journey in one place: search, financing and brokerage. We started from nothing, and six months later the product was ready for investor demos and pilot users.
owned: Core user flows for brokers and buyers
Dashboards for each type of profile
projects.team: I worked directly with the CEO and the CTO, fully remote from Spain.

outcomes.label: months from zero to a product ready for investor demos and pilot users

chapters.title: Dashboards and analytics
body: I designed two dashboard views: one for the activity of a single franchise, and one for several franchises at once.
Each view changes with the role of the person using it and shows the data that role needs. I kept the charts readable for every level of user.

chapters.title: Core flows
body: I designed the main flows of the MVP for property search, financing and document management, with as little friction as possible between brokers and buyers.

I mapped each journey end to end and paid close attention to the moments when one profile hands over to another. Buying a property is complicated, so the product had to feel approachable from day one.

projects.name: Vibe
projects.summary: I owned the core flows and built the design system the product needed to keep growing.
projects.tagline: Reworking the core of a fast-growing ad-tech platform.

facts.Scope: Design system, Product design, SaaS design

projects.intro: Vibe is like Google Ads for TV: any marketer can plan, buy and air TV ads on major channels in a few minutes. There was already an MVP when I joined. My job was to rework the main flows and give the product a base it could grow on.
owned: The design system, documented in Storybook
projects.team: A small team of about 10 people, split between Paris and the US. I worked fully remote from Spain.

outcomes.label: months shipping new features in short sprints

chapters.title: Campaign dashboard and creation flow
body: I started with the whole campaign experience, from creation to tracking. We simplified the flow so people could build and manage campaigns faster and still stay in control.
The new dashboard shows active campaigns and their main metrics more clearly. I redesigned creation step by step, with simpler targeting, audience selection and scheduling.

chapters.title: Campaign views and analytics
body: Once creation was stable, we moved on to management views and analytics. People needed to check performance across several campaigns and act on it from the same place.
I designed table views with filters and custom sorting, and a new analytics dashboard built for comparing campaigns, so people can decide from the data.

chapters.title: User management and permissions
body: I also designed user management, team access and billing, so the product works for every kind of organisation, from independent agencies to large brands.
I documented every component and behaviour in Storybook, which kept handoff to the engineers clean and consistent.

projects.name: 360Learning
projects.summary: With my squad, I owned the enterprise suite, and I helped keep the shared design system in good shape.
projects.tagline: Faster, simpler course creation for more than 1,700 enterprise clients.

facts.Scope: Product design, Design system, Web design, SaaS design

projects.intro: 360Learning is a collaborative learning platform that companies use to build and share knowledge internally. I spent more than three years there as a product designer in the Enterprise squad, where my main job was designing and growing the enterprise suite.
owned: Learning Needs, from first request to course creation
projects.team: My squad was one PM and two developers. Around us was a design team of eight, each person owning a different part of the product.

outcomes.label: less time to create a course

chapters.title: Learning Needs
body: This was the first feature I worked on. With Learning Needs, employees say what they want to learn and find colleagues who have the expertise.

When someone posts a need, others can upvote it, join the discussion or volunteer to create the course. We designed the whole experience, from collecting requests to finding contributors and running the collaboration, so that learning inside a company would be more social and easier to see.

chapters.title: Course structure and draft management
body: Once a need is approved, the team starts building the course. This step is about planning, organising and assigning the work before creation starts.
We designed a simple interface to manage drafts and set the structure. It shows who owns each step, so everyone knows before creation begins.

chapters.title: Design system
body: With eight designers each owning a different area, we needed a shared system to stay consistent. Regular syncs between squads helped us spot new patterns early, before they split into several versions.

The system grew from basic atoms to complex patterns like modals, forms and data tables. I worked closely with developers on handoff standards, usage guidelines and edge cases. Keeping it healthy meant reviewing new requests all the time so nothing got built twice.

projects.name: AXA
projects.summary: As a consultant, I designed new features and system components, and helped designers and developers work from the same language.
projects.tagline: One design language for AXA’s insurance and banking products.

facts.Role: Consulting product designer, through Monsieur Guiz
facts.Scope: Design system, Product design, App design, Illustration

projects.intro: AXA is one of the largest insurance and banking groups in the world, present in more than 50 countries. Through the agency Monsieur Guiz, I worked as a consulting product designer on both sides of the business, on new features, the design system and a product language the teams could share.
owned: New features for the AXA Insurance website
The website presenting the new AXA Bank app
Components and documentation in the shared design system
projects.team: I consulted through the agency Monsieur Guiz: six months with AXA Bank and six months with AXA Insurance, working close to the development teams.

chapters.title: Insurance and bank websites
body: At AXA Insurance, I designed new features for the website and improved the foundations of the design system: layouts, navigation and responsive guidelines that work across products and devices.
For AXA Bank, I designed the responsive layouts and visuals of a website presenting the new mobile app. The features had to be easy to understand, and the site had to stay true to the brand.

chapters.title: Design system
body: I contributed to the shared AXA Design System by building components and defining the spacing, constraints and documentation the development teams worked from.
Each component had to behave the same way across teams and contexts, and still leave room to adapt.

chapters.title: Illustrations
body: Alongside the product work, I drew a set of custom illustrations for the AXA Bank website and app.
They explain complicated financial topics in a friendlier way and make the product easier to approach for everyday users.

pages.title: About
pages.metaDescription: Nicolas Milosevic, senior product designer based in Spain, with nine years in fast-moving teams across Europe.
pages.heading: Nine years of untangling products with the people who build them.
intro: I’m Nicolas, a senior product designer based in Spain. For nine years I’ve worked with fast-moving teams across Europe, from early-stage startups to large companies.

Most of my work is making complicated products easier to use. Sometimes that’s a full platform redesign, sometimes a single feature or a design system. Whatever the size, I start with a clear structure, and then I take care of the details.
I’m comfortable leading design from start to finish, and just as happy being one voice in a good team. My best work came from working every day with people who saw the problem differently from me.

items.title: I own the outcome
items.body: When I take on a product area, it’s mine from end to end: the structure, the flows, the details and the questions nobody else has time for. I stay on it until it ships.

items.title: I design with the people who build
items.body: I work closely with founders, product managers and engineers. Most good decisions come out of those conversations, so I bring people in early and show work before it’s finished.

items.title: I leave a system behind
items.body: Every project on this site has a design system, because the team has to keep shipping after I leave. It lets them keep using our decisions when I’m not around.

items.title: I work remotely and stay close
items.body: For years I’ve worked from Spain with teams in Paris, the US and elsewhere. Clear files, written decisions and being easy to reach keep the distance from getting in the way.
